changes: Implemented the B-f57a M1 cross_host_review hardening: host-A and host-B local verdicts are built as one pair, guarded before and after write, deleted on final HEAD/source drift, and process events append only after the final guard. Updated the cross-host smoke to cover post-write clean HEAD drift cleanup and refreshed all story evidence.
usage: Run lattice cross_host_review for a REVIEW story with an authorized review-only dispatch policy and host-A findings; use node packages/main/dist/tasks/cross-host-review-smoke.js for deterministic local verification of the command surface and fail-closed cases.
expectedOutcome: cross_host_review records structured material-bound host verdicts, surfaces host disagreement, and refuses dirty/source-drift/head-drift/malformed-output paths without retaining stale or partial verdicts.
actualTranscript: npm --prefix packages/main run build passed; node packages/main/dist/tasks/cross-host-review-smoke.js passed 24/24; lattice validate --story=B-f57a --json passed 32/32 configured commands; evidence_plan reports 24 fresh, 0 missing, 0 rerun, 0 refreshOnly; reviewer lanes concept/test-coverage/quality passed as RP-011/RP-012/RP-013.
outcomeDiff: No acceptance diff. Actual matched expected; the suite now includes the additional F-016 post-write clean HEAD drift cleanup proof.
limitations: Live external two-host Codex CLI proof-of-mechanism remains the separate M3 milestone; this M1 story proves the local orchestrator, structured verdict capture, drift guards, and disagreement logic with deterministic injected seams.
pitfalls: The main pitfall was repeated stale reviewer/evidence cycles after F-016. The final fix had to treat the two local host verdict files as a pair and delay process-event append until after the post-write drift guard; future changes should keep that ordering.
